name: Rabbit Ears
summary: Free live TV for Omarchy: hundreds of public channels, a live programme guide and favourites, no account needed
description:
New in 1.4.0: Cast, Pop-out, and Quality buttons right in the player. Pick higher quality (720p, 1080p) when available.

Rabbit Ears turns your Omarchy computer into a TV. Open it and you're watching: news, sport, music, kids, movies and local channels from the USA, UK, Canada, Australia and 70+ more countries. No account, no subscription, nothing to sign up for.

WATCH
• Hundreds of free channels, checked every hour so dead ones disappear by themselves.
• Click a channel and it plays. Up and down arrows change channel, like a remote.
• Full screen with a double-click or F. Mute with M.

WHAT'S ON
• Press G for the guide: what's playing now and what's next, channel by channel. Click a programme to jump straight to it.
• The now-playing bar shows the current programme and its times.

MAKE IT YOURS
• Hold a channel (or press ★) to add it to your favourites. They get their own tab.
• Search by name, or browse by country or by type: News, Sports, Kids, Music, Movies.
• The colours follow your Omarchy theme.

WHERE THE CHANNELS COME FROM
The list comes from the Free-TV/IPTV project, which only includes channels that the broadcaster itself gives away for free (free-to-air and ad-supported stations). Rabbit Ears hosts, records and re-streams nothing: it plays each broadcaster's own public address, exactly as a web browser would. Some channels only play in their home country; those are marked.

changelog.title: The guide stays live
items: The programme guide refreshes every 20 minutes while the app is open, instead of only at launch
If the guide is nearly exhausted — after a sleep or a dropped connection — it refreshes immediately
The store publishes 36 hours of guide instead of 14, refreshed every 4 hours instead of daily

changelog.title: New logo
items: New logo: the approved retro TV design, on the app, launcher and dock.

changelog.title: Player buttons & quality picker
items: Cast, Pop-out, and Quality buttons now right in the player - no keyboard shortcuts needed.
Quality picker: click HD to see all sources for a channel and pick higher resolution (720p, 1080p) when available.
Press Q to open the quality picker.

changelog.title: Cast to your TV
items: Press C (or tap 📡) to find Chromecast, Roku, and DLNA smart TVs on your network. Click a device and the channel plays on your TV.
Pop-out mini player: Press P and the picture floats in a corner above everything. Drag it anywhere, scroll to resize, double-click to bring the app back.

changelog.title: Pop-out mini player
items: Press P (or the ⧉ button): the picture pops out into a small window that stays on top of everything. Drag it anywhere, scroll to make it bigger or smaller, double-click to bring the full app back.

changelog.title: Never a dead channel
items: Up to 5 feeds per channel (the broadcaster's own, Pluto TV, Samsung TV Plus, Plex, Roku…). If one freezes or buffers, Rabbit Ears switches to the next by itself.
Source pill in the player shows which feed is playing; click it or press S to switch.
New Movies and Series tabs: free film and TV-show channels from licensed free platforms.
Update available button in the app: one click installs the newest version.
New icon.

changelog.title: First release
items: Hundreds of free public channels from 70+ countries, refreshed hourly.
What's on guide with now and next, click to watch.
Favourites, search, country and genre tabs.
Full screen, mute, remote-style channel up/down.

featured.headline: Hundreds of TV channels. Free. No account.
featured.tagline: News, sport, music, kids and movies from 70+ countries, with a live guide of what's on. Click a channel and you're watching. Open source, nothing to sign up for.

features.title: Just press play
features.body: Open Rabbit Ears and it's already playing. A grid of channels with their logos on the left, the picture on the right. Click any channel to switch; arrow keys work like a remote.

features.title: Never a dead channel
features.body: Every channel can have several feeds behind it. If the one you're watching freezes or buffers, Rabbit Ears quietly switches to the next. Press S to switch yourself.

features.title: Pop it out
features.body: Press P and the picture floats in a corner, on top of everything, while you work. Drag it anywhere, scroll to resize, double-click to come back.

features.title: Cast to your TV
features.body: Press C to find Chromecast, Roku, and DLNA smart TVs on your network. Click a device and the channel plays on your TV while you keep working.

features.title: What's on, right now
features.body: Press G and see what's playing now and what's next on every channel that publishes a guide. Click a programme and you're watching it.

features.title: Favourites and search
features.body: Hold a channel to make it a favourite; they get their own tab. Search by name, or flick through countries and genres: News, Sports, Kids, Music, Movies.

features.title: Full screen or a corner
features.body: Double-click for full screen, or keep it small in the corner while you work. The window is yours to size and move.

features.title: Always fresh
features.body: The channel list and guide are rebuilt every hour by the Omarchy Store. Every stream is checked first, so channels that go dark drop out on their own.

features.title: Looks like it belongs
features.body: Colours follow your Omarchy theme, so it matches the rest of your desktop whatever theme you pick.

steps.title: Install it
steps.body: Press GET in the Omarchy Store app, or use the install options above. Type your password when asked.

steps.title: Open Rabbit Ears
steps.body: Press Super + Space, type Rabbit, press Enter. It starts on a channel straight away.

steps.title: Find something to watch
steps.body: Pick a country or genre at the top, press G for the guide, and hold a channel to add it to your favourites.

faq.a: Yes. Rabbit Ears only lists channels the broadcaster itself gives away for free, from the Free-TV/IPTV project, and plays each one from the broadcaster's own public address, like a web browser would. It hosts, records and re-streams nothing.
Some broadcasters only allow viewing in their own country; those channels are marked. Others go off air now and then; the list is re-checked every hour and dead channels drop out.

faq.q: Is there a guide for every channel?
faq.a: The big US, UK, Canadian and Australian channels have a now-and-next guide. Many smaller stations don't publish one, so they show their country or genre instead.
No. Rabbit Ears is free and open source (MIT).

promise.title: Free, open source, no account.
promise.body: Rabbit Ears is free to use and free to look inside. There's no sign-up, no tracking and nothing to pay, now or later.

install.note: Needs Quickshell and Qt Multimedia (the installer adds them if they're missing). Nothing else on your system is changed.
